The conference features discussions on data sharing regimes, content moderation, the role of technology in shaping social identities, and the ethical implications of AI and automation.

title: Smart Cities and National Security
keywords: smart cities; national security; data governance; cyber security; critical infrastructure; privacy; data breach; risk assessment; supply chain; espionage
abstract: This document outlines the concept of smart cities, their implementation in Canada, and associated national security concerns. Smart cities, which utilize digital technologies to enhance municipal services, collect and analyze data through connected sensors and devices. The document highlights potential threats such as data exploitation, interconnected critical infrastructure vulnerabilities, and methods of compromise, including cyber operations and supply chain risks. Key considerations for smart city adoption emphasize data governance, security best practices, citizen engagement, transparency, vendor due diligence, risk assessments, and incident response planning.

authors: Robert D. Atkinson; William C. Mayville; Emily Rauhala; Hirobumi Kayama; Matthew P. Goodman; Jonathan E. Hillman; Kate O‚ÄôKeeffe

abstract: This transcript captures a CSIS event discussing China's Digital Silk Road initiative. Speakers address the initiative's components: telecommunications infrastructure, e-commerce, and smart city projects, with emphasis on US-Japan collaboration given technological advancements in Asia. Concerns about China's dominance in setting technology standards, data access, and potential military implications are raised. The discussion also covers Huawei's role, its impact on global 5G, and security risks. The panel analyzes the initiative's broader strategic implications, the necessity for the U.S. and its allies to present alternatives, and how to respond effectively, including commercial strategies and data localization.

title: The Rise of Chinese AI in the Gulf: a Renewal of China‚Äôs ‚ÄòSerbia Model‚Äô
authors: Wendy Robinson
keywords: china; artificial intelligence; gulf states; serbia; military technology; smart cities; uav; technology transfer; foreign policy; international relations
abstract: This policy analysis examines China's growing influence in the Gulf region through the export of advanced technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), smart city infrastructure, and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). It argues that China is replicating a model pioneered in Serbia, where technology transfers led to increased military collaboration. The Gulf states, with their wealth and strategic locations, are becoming key markets for Chinese technology. The analysis suggests that the United States can counter China's growing influence by offering diverse, high-quality technology options, addressing export restrictions, and highlighting the security risks associated with Chinese technology.

title: BCDA 2016 Annual Report
authors: Rodrigo Roa Duterte; Gregorio D. Garcia III; Vivencio B. Dizon; Paterno Morales; Delfin Lorenzana; Restituto F. Padilla Jr.; Jessica Bautista-Padilla; Ruth Valdevilla; Ferdinand Golez; Allan Garcia; E

BCDA remitted Php4 billion to the Bureau of Treasury, with Php3.6 billion allocated for AFP modernization. The report details BCDA's involvement in infrastructure projects such as the BGC-NAIA Bus Rapid Transit System, Subic-Clark Cargo Railway, Clark International Airport expansion, and the development of New Clark City. The report also underscores BCDA's focus on sustainable and smart city development, as well as its corporate social responsibility efforts benefiting the military and local communities.

title: 40 Years of Digital Innovation and Activism in Manchester: From Urban Telematics to Smart Cities
authors: Dave Carter
keywords: smart cities; digital innovation; activism; telematics; manchester; community networks; open innovation; living labs; ict
abstract: This document chronicles Manchester's evolution as a "modern internet city" over four decades, tracing its journey from early digital innovation and activism to its current status as a "smart city." It highlights key developments such as the Poptel project, the Manchester Host Computer Communications & Information Network, the establishment of community ICT access centers, and the city's role in the "Information City" and "Smart City" initiatives. The text also touches upon the influence of academic and military research, activist networking, the digital divide, and the emergence of user-generated content. It emphasizes Manchester's pioneering efforts in digital infrastructure, community engagement, and open innovation, including its participation in European smart city networks and the "Living Lab" concept.

title: National Timing Centre Programme: Building a Resilient Time Infrastructure for the UK
keywords: time distribution; national timing centre; npl; gnss vulnerability; resilience; atomic clocks; synchronization; critical infrastructure; uk
abstract: The National Timing Centre (NTC) programme, led by the National Physical Laboratory (NPL), aims to establish a trusted and assured time and frequency distribution system across the UK. Recognizing the vulnerabilities of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) and the increasing reliance on precise timing data for critical infrastructure, digital services, and emerging technologies like autonomous vehicles and smart cities, the NTC programme seeks to provide a resilient alternative. It will leverage multiple time distribution technologies, including fiber, satellites, and terrestrial broadcasts, alongside GNSS. The program also includes developing a new atomic clock network, fostering innovation through partnerships with Innovate UK, and addressing skills shortages in the field. This initiative is crucial for national security, economic stability, and technological advancement.

title: Privacy Challenges and Big Data in Smart City
authors: Iam-chong Ip; King-Wa Fu; Yuk-ming Leung; Kai-chi Leung
keywords: smart city; big data; privacy; surveillance; data protection; hong kong; public policy; regulation
abstract: This research report examines the privacy challenges posed by big data and smart city initiatives in Hong Kong. It highlights a significant gap between current governance mechanisms and public expectations regarding data privacy, particularly concerning government surveillance. The study analyzes two case studies: the "Multi-functional Smart Lampposts" pilot scheme and a facial recognition access system in a residential estate. It finds that existing regulations, like the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance, are insufficient to address new forms of personal data and the concerns surrounding surveillance states. The report recommends rebuilding public trust, enacting legislation to limit government data processing, mandating privacy impact assessments, improving data transparency, and establishing an independent body to oversee national security-related data collection.

title: Who Buys and Controls CCTV? Myanmar's Slippery Slope to Mass Surveillance
authors: ARTICLE 19; Digital Rights Collective
keywords: cctv; myanmar; surveillance; mass surveillance; human rights; privacy; freedom of expression; smart cities; data protection; procurement
abstract: This report by ARTICLE 19 and Digital Rights Collective investigates the procurement and deployment of Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) systems in Myanmar, focusing on Mandalay, Yangon, and Naypyidaw. It highlights concerns about transparency, accountability, and the human rights implications of CCTV infrastructure, especially in the context of the 2021 military coup. The study reveals how CCTV systems, often procured through opaque processes with significant involvement from companies like Huawei, are becoming the foundation for mass surveillance and AI-driven technologies. The report emphasizes the lack of data protection frameworks and the erosion of freedoms of expression, privacy, and assembly due to the expanding surveillance network. Recommendations are provided for the military junta and private sector to ensure rights-respecting smart city development.
